_notes: Fuel use model: fuel per hour = a x rated kW + b x output kW. For each fuel, a + b = 3.6 / (full_load_efficiency x energy_mj_per_unit), and a = no_load_fraction x (a + b). Diesel values reproduce the HOMER manual's worked example (50 kW generator: 8.48 L/hr at 25 kW, 15.3 L/hr at 50 kW). Values marked approximate are typical figures, not measurements: replace them with your generator's spec sheet where you can.
no_load_fraction_source: HOMER manual example: intercept 0.033 L/hr/kW rated, slope 0.273 L/hr/kW, so 0.033 / (0.033 + 0.273) = 0.108

diesel.name: Diesel (AGO)
diesel.source: Efficiency derived from the HOMER manual worked example (15.3 L/hr at 50 kW) with diesel at 36 MJ/L (Engineering ToolBox)

petrol.name: Petrol (PMS)
petrol.source: Approximate: petrol about 43-44 MJ/kg at 0.74 kg/L; efficiency typical of small spark-ignition generators

lpg.name: LPG (cooking gas)
lpg.source: Approximate: LPG 46-51 MJ/kg (lower end used); efficiency typical of gas spark-ignition generators

cng.name: CNG (compressed natural gas)
cng.source: Approximate: natural gas about 37 MJ/scm gross, about 34 MJ/scm net; efficiency typical of gas generators

pipeline_gas.name: Pipeline natural gas
pipeline_gas.source: Approximate: same gas as CNG; larger pipeline-fed gas generators are usually more efficient

mmbtu_per_scm_source: Approximate: natural gas 37.3 MJ/scm gross (FAO) / 1,055.06 MJ per MMBtu
